stem: An unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant client asks when Rho(D) immune globulin is routinely given. Which response is correct?

options.A: It is routinely given at 26–28 weeks of gestation and again after delivery if the newborn is Rh-positive.
options.B: It is given only after delivery and never during pregnancy.
options.C: It is given only during the first trimester.
options.D: It is routinely given after delivery only when the newborn is Rh-negative.

rationale: Rho(D) immune globulin labeling recommends antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks for appropriate unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant clients. A postpartum dose is indicated when the newborn is Rh-positive.
educational_objective: State the routine antepartum and postpartum timing of Rho(D) immune globulin.
source_locator: Dosage and Administration—Antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks; Postpartum if newborn is Rh-positive
source_claim_supported: RhoGAM is given at 26–28 weeks for routine antepartum prophylaxis and postpartum when the newborn is Rh-positive.
correction_summary: Corrected 'around 28 weeks' to the exact labeled 26–28 week interval.
audit_findings: Distractors conflict with labeled antepartum/postpartum use.
Independent second pass found a unique answer.
